context: Meridian Freight Systems: Series B logistics SaaS, ~$31M ARR, planning to raise a Series C in October. The board cares about the fundraise story, customer concentration, and whether the enterprise pivot is real.
headline: Cash runway is roughly 8 months at current burn. 3 critical and 7 high risks are live; 3 opportunities.
summary: Revenue is growing (18% on the period), but gross margin, nps, deferred revenue, burn, dso, concentration all moved the wrong way in the same period. The advisor's reading: the growth story is masking a concentration and reliability problem that could unwind quickly. 8 assumptions in the leadership narrative do not survive the evidence.

risks.title: Cash runway is roughly 8 months at current burn
risks.rationale: Cash $14.6M against burn $1.9M per month gives about 7.7 months — under the 12-month floor most boards require before a raise.
risks.action: Rebuild the cash forecast on current burn with no unsigned expansion revenue, and set a burn ceiling
objections: contrarian (sustain): Evidence is consistent across sources.

risks.title: Top customer is 34% of ARR
risks.rationale: Single-customer share is 34%, up from 19%. Losing or renegotiating that account moves the whole plan. The same customer holds a contractual exit right.
risks.action: Cap the single-customer share of ARR in the plan and put a second-account expansion programme behind it
objections: contrarian (sustain): Evidence is consistent across sources.

risks.title: Repeated outages on the core subsystem have triggered a customer's termination right
risks.rationale: 3 incidents recorded on the same subsystem; SLA credits of $212k. The third breach in a rolling window activates termination for convenience.
risks.action: Freeze feature work on the affected subsystem, fill the open platform reqs, and put a change-management gate on production migrations
objections: contrarian (sustain): Evidence is consistent across sources.

risks.title: A key renewal is being forecast on a relationship that no longer exists
risks.rationale: The champion has left and the replacement is not engaging, yet the deal is still forecast at a high probability.
risks.action: Get an executive sponsor in front of the new decision-maker at the at-risk account before the renewal date
objections: contrarian (sustain): Evidence is consistent across sources.

risks.title: Top-quartile sales reps are leaving
risks.rationale: Regretted attrition in the sales team, with a comp-plan change named as the cause.
risks.action: Review the comp plan change with the remaining top-quartile reps and correct it before more leave
objections: contrarian (sustain): Evidence is consistent across sources.

risks.title: Customer sentiment falling: NPS 31 from 47
risks.rationale: A 16-point NPS drop in one period, with detractors citing reliability and a perceived shift of focus to one customer.
risks.action: Run a detractor call programme with the enterprise segment and publish a reliability commitment
objections: contrarian (sustain): Evidence is consistent across sources.

risks.title: Gross margin fell 5 points
risks.rationale: Margin moved from 66% to 61%. If onboarding cost is structural rather than one-off, the enterprise model is less profitable than presented.
risks.action: Separate one-off onboarding cost from structural margin and decide which it is
objections: contrarian (sustain): Evidence is consistent across sources.

risks.title: Burn rate up 46% quarter on quarter
risks.rationale: Monthly burn rose from $1.3M to $1.9M, ahead of any signed expansion revenue.
risks.action: Tie further hiring to signed, not verbal, revenue
objections: contrarian (sustain): Evidence is consistent across sources.

risks.title: SMB customers are asking how to leave
risks.rationale: Annual-plan customers asking about early termination is a leading churn indicator, coinciding with a deliberate deprioritisation of that segment.
risks.action: Call every SMB account that asked about leaving, and reverse the SMB feature freeze until the enterprise expansion is signed
objections: contrarian (sustain): Evidence is consistent across sources.

risks.title: The platform team is a single point of failure
risks.rationale: One engineer has carried every incident and has flagged burnout; open platform reqs have gone unfilled for months.
risks.action: Rotate on-call this week and backfill the platform team before anything else
objections: contrarian (sustain): Evidence is consistent across sources.

risks.title: Collections slowing: DSO 71 days from 48
risks.rationale: Cash is arriving later while burn is rising; combined with renewals moving to monthly billing this compounds the runway problem.
risks.action: Move the accounts that switched to monthly billing back to annual prepay at renewal, with a discount if needed
objections: contrarian (sustain): Evidence is consistent across sources.

risks.title: A competitor is targeting the installed base with a free migration tool
risks.rationale: Customers are raising the competitor unprompted on calls.
risks.action: Build a retention offer for the mid-market base the competitor is targeting
objections: contrarian (sustain): Evidence is consistent across sources.

risks.title: Headcount grew 20% while revenue grew 18%
risks.rationale: Cost is scaling faster than revenue; the productivity story has to be shown, not assumed.
risks.action: Pause non-critical hiring until revenue growth exceeds headcount growth
objections: contrarian (sustain): Evidence is consistent across sources.

opportunities.title: Inbound demand is rising; conversion is the fixable bottleneck
opportunities.rationale: Lead volume is up sharply while conversion fell from 11% to 6%. Recovering conversion on the higher volume is cheaper growth than any new channel.
opportunities.action: A/B test the pricing page change against the previous version and fix conversion before blaming lead quality
objections: contrarian (sustain): Evidence is consistent across sources.

opportunities.title: A large expansion is on the table
opportunities.rationale: An expansion of this size would materially lift ARR — if it closes.
opportunities.action: Get the expansion order form signed before any plan depends on it
objections: contrarian (weaken): The expansion is a verbal commitment described as 'just paperwork'; nothing is signed and the plan already depends on it.

opportunities.title: Customers can quantify the savings the product delivers
opportunities.rationale: Promoters cite hard savings and a strong onboarding team — the retention message is already written by customers.
opportunities.action: Turn the quantified savings customers report into a retention and renewal message
objections: contrarian (weaken): Rests on a single qualitative line of evidence; no number behind it yet.

assumptions.why_questionable: On the numbers in the same document, $14.6M of cash at $1.9M per month is about 7.7 months — not 'comfortably above 12'.
assumptions.test: Rebuild the cash forecast on current burn with unsigned expansion excluded; compare to the board deck figure.

assumptions.statement: The reliability problems are growing pains that the platform team has under control
assumptions.why_questionable: 3 incidents on the same subsystem, one engineer on call for all of them flagging burnout, and open reqs unfilled for months is not 'under control'; it is a team at capacity.
assumptions.test: Ask for the incident trend by week and the on-call roster for the last 90 days.

assumptions.statement: The expansion will close this quarter because procurement is 'just paperwork'
assumptions.why_questionable: A verbal yes from an operations VP is not a signature, and the same customer has just escalated a third SLA breach to the CEO and holds a termination right.
assumptions.test: Ask procurement for the signed order form date; until then move the deal out of Commit.

assumptions.statement: The at-risk renewal is still a 90% probability
assumptions.why_questionable: The champion left in July and the new decision-maker is not returning calls; a 90% forecast is inertia, not evidence.
assumptions.test: Re-forecast at 50% until the new VP takes a meeting; get an executive sponsor to request one this week.

assumptions.statement: Enterprise customer-success hiring will be paid back by expansion revenue
assumptions.why_questionable: The expansion is unsigned and concentration is already 34%; the cost is certain and the revenue is not.
assumptions.test: Model CS cost against signed expansion only and show the payback period.

assumptions.statement: Engineering headcount can wait until after the raise
assumptions.why_questionable: The reliability incidents are the thing most likely to derail the raise; deferring the fix until after it is circular.
assumptions.test: Cost two platform hires against one more SLA breach with the top customer.

assumptions.statement: Q2 was the best quarter ever
assumptions.why_questionable: Revenue grew, but margin, burn, DSO, deferred revenue and NPS all moved the wrong way in the same quarter. Best by one metric, worst by five.
assumptions.test: Put the six metrics side by side on one slide and ask the board which quarter it prefers.

assumptions.statement: Inbound conversion fell because the leads are lower quality
assumptions.why_questionable: Conversion halved immediately after a pricing page change; lead quality is the explanation that requires no one to have made a mistake.
assumptions.test: Restore the previous pricing page for half the traffic for two weeks and compare conversion.

Ask for the incident trend by week and the on-call roster for the last 90 days.
Ask procurement for the signed order form date; until then move the deal out of Commit.
Re-forecast at 50% until the new VP takes a meeting; get an executive sponsor to request one this week.
Model CS cost against signed expansion only and show the payback period.
What is net revenue retention by segment, and what was it last quarter?
gaps: Gross and net revenue retention by segment — the brief cannot tell whether growth is new logos or expansion
Pipeline coverage and stage-weighted forecast, not verbal commitments
A 12-month cash forecast that separates signed from unsigned revenue
